newsitem.title: FRANCE: Left to seize majority in French 1998 vote - poll.
newsitem.headline: Left to seize majority in French 1998 vote - poll.

text.p: France's left is set to win a majority in 1998 general elections, forcing conservative president Jacques Chirac into "cohabitation" with an opposition prime minister, an opinion poll released on Tuesday showed.

The poll, to be published in the bi-monthly "Politique Opinion," showed the left winning 293 National Assembly seats and the right 262 out of 555 seats for metropolitan France. The poll did not include the 22 seats for overseas territories.
The right now has 480 out of 577 lower house seats won at the last general election in March 1993, when Socialist President Francois Mitterrand was in power and his popularity was steadily falling.
Chirac was elected in May 1995 with nearly 53 percent of the vote but his popularity has plummeted since, due to a series of crippling strikes over taxes and pension rights last winter.
If the results given by the Tuesday poll were confirmed in 1998, Chirac would have to pick a prime minister and cabinet from the opposition, which could paralyse his presidency.

His own popularity and that of fellow Gaullist Alain Juppe's cabinet has continued to drop since last winter over their failure to check unemployment, now at over three million, and a series of moves seen by the public as hitting family incomes.
The opinion poll was conducted by the CSA group on October 25-26 among 1,004 people.
